posts.name: speedyolrac
posts.cooked:
Not too bad,I love DW crew, even if they are tough to play with. Keeping up the Mysterious Ceremonies up is important, they need more plays and draws. Just bank on you winning before you die. Setback and Nightmist where support, set back healed and prevented 20+ damage. Nightmist board wipe a few times and prevent the boss from playing cards. DW Nightmist requires loads of planning and knowledge of what might be needed next turn. Both feed the angry Fixer. A double shot of nitrogen round kept a dangerous round from being to hurting too much. 

I play this group often so I know their limitations and how to work around them. I didn't shuffle any deck so Handelbra could have done worst. Getting Expat to unload on the environment deck was a keep play. My team as at 12+ hp expat took her out with her handgun.

posts.name: rjc917
posts.cooked:
Well that was a slog, but I got the mint.  I had things set up for Fixer to take out the Cohorts (and pretty much everything else) on his turn, but then the Matriarch started horrifically screeching a cacophony, killing an Apprentice Poisoner, who got revenge by killing off her giant flock of birds.  And since Odin's ravens hadn't been destroyed yet, my heroes were taking a boosted 4 damage for each bird destroyed.  So after all that, everyone but Nightmist was dead, and she was at 2 hp.

Needless to say, Nightmist immediately turned to mist.  And thus began the long process of healing with Starshield Necklace, performing Mysterious Ceremonies to draw lots of cards, and repeatedly reviving Expatriette.  I knew that if I got Matriarch to be lower than me, I could get Zhu Long to start attacking her, but she was at 50 or so hp when this started, so I had a ways to go.

I finally took her out, taking her from the mid 20s to 0 hp in one round.  I became a Master of Magic on my turn to help get my hp above hers.  Then I used my three Mysterious Ceremonies plays to unleash a Heedless Lash which put the Amulet in play, Mistbound Matriarch's deck so she couldn't cause any trouble, and send everything into Obliveon, including three Shinobi Assassins, which leapt off of my deck to finish off the wounded Matriarch when Setback motivated me to use my power.

I don't like Dark Watch or the Matriarch (unless Tachyon is around), and I really thought I had no chance of winning with the way this started out, but this ended up being one of the most intense games of Sentinels I've ever played.

posts.name: robb8888
posts.cooked:
How did anybody beat this, much less get Mint?  

 

I tried getting rid of the Mask, only to have Huginn and Cacophony take away all of my extra ongoings so Nightmist couldn't peer into Matriarch's deck, and Fixer had no extra stuff to destroy.  I tried getting rid of Huginn, but Muninn came out I tried not destroying Mysterious Ceremonies...only to have it pull out the Ninja and the Poisoner, who proceeded to kill off birds, and consequently my heroes.  Between Huginn and the *conveniently* placed Cacophonies, there's virtually no way to keep Nightmist's Astral Projection out long enough to keep the Matriarch's deck in control.  The Darken the Skies are evenly spread out in the deck, so that even if you do manage to get rid of the Mask...and Huginn...and Muninn...and Carrion Fields....the two Darken the Skies come out and just make you start all over again.   I'm on my 10th try trying to beat this, and still haven't made it past Round 4.

 

And as for the comment that the decks are rarely "rigged," the Darken The Skies just happen to be evenly spaced throughout the deck, and Setback just happens to be laden with useless cards that require him to discard unlucky points, but no cards that let him *add* lucky points, and both Fixer and Expatriette's only weapons in their deck just *happen* to be the "damage everything" weapons which are the worst to use against the Matriarch??!
